bibliographic.title: Reporting Guidelines for Artificial Intelligence Studies in Healthcare (for Both Conventional and Large Language Models): What's New in 2024
bibliographic.authors: Seong Ho Park, Chong Hyun Suh
bibliographic.citation_apa: Park, S. H., & Suh, C. H. (2024). Reporting Guidelines for Artificial Intelligence Studies in Healthcare (for Both Conventional and Large Language Models): What's New in 2024. Korean Journal of Radiology, 25(8), 687-690. https://doi.org/10.3348/kjr.2024.0598

methodology.technology_context: Reporting guidelines for AI and LLM studies in healthcare (TRIPOD+AI, CLAIM 2024, CHART in development); recommendations for transparency and reproducibility in LLM research reporting including chatbots and prompting

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed editorial summarizing 2024 updates to healthcare AI reporting guidelines (TRIPOD+AI, CLAIM) and offering minimum recommendations for LLM study reporting, including LLM-linked chatbots and CHART. It addresses transparency and reproducibility in research reporting rather than operational conversational governance, guardrails, oversight, audit, or compliance of deployed LLM conversational systems in regulated settings. Relevant as foundational/contextual evidence on reporting transparency for LLM chatbot studies in healthcare.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python triage scored central_candidate (90.67/A), but the full text is an editorial on research reporting guidelines, not empirical or operational conversational governance; adjudication should confirm foundational vs supporting classification.

appraisal.notes: Editorial without empirical sampling or primary data collection; appraised as narrative guideline synthesis. Strengths: clear objectives, structured recommendations (Table 2), citation of established guidelines. Weaknesses for governance review: no evaluation of deployed conversational systems, oversight mechanisms, or operational risk controls.

cerqual.explanation: Coherent editorial synthesis with explicit LLM and chatbot reporting recommendations in a regulated healthcare context. Limited direct relevance to operational conversational governance because focus is research reporting quality, not deployment supervision, audit, or compliance controls.

coding.theme: Transparency and reproducibility standards for reporting healthcare AI and LLM research
coding.subtheme: LLM and chatbot study reporting recommendations

synthesis.main_claim: Updated healthcare AI reporting guidelines (TRIPOD+AI, CLAIM 2024) address model development and performance reporting, while separate minimum recommendations are needed for LLM studies—including chatbot evaluations—covering test data independence, prompt transparency, stochasticity, and session design.
synthesis.contribution: Concise 2024 update on healthcare AI reporting guidelines and actionable minimum recommendations (Table 2) to improve transparency and reproducibility in LLM research reports, including LLM-linked chatbots via emerging CHART.
synthesis.limitations: Editorial format without systematic review methods; does not address operational governance, deployment monitoring, human oversight, or audit of live conversational systems; several issues noted as still unaddressed in latest guideline updates.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational/contextual evidence on transparency and reporting standards for LLM and chatbot studies in regulated healthcare; not central evidence for operational conversational governance frameworks.
